editorial.tldr: September's recursive self-improvement (RSI) papers retrained models on their own output; November's wave instead has agents rewrite their harness (prompts, tools, memory, control loop) with the base model frozen. Early November added a benchmark for that loop, a statistical-guarantee method to keep it trustworthy, and a multi-agent version for closed-loop science.
editorial.whats_new: Two Nov 18 papers push RSI back into the weights: BaseRSI internalizes harness gains into a base vision-language model without training, and Piccolo co-evolves 0.8B-27B decision models with their own training data.
editorial.why_it_matters: Harness-level RSI means an agent can change its own prompts, tools, and memory in production, so the harness itself becomes a versioned artifact that needs evals and rollback.
editorial.take_for_builders: If your agent edits its own prompts, tools, or memory, version every self-edit and gate it on a held-out eval with a rollback path before it reaches production.

beats.headline: Harness RSI gets a benchmark and a statistical safety check
beats.summary: Flex-RSI scores how well frontier agents improve their own harness; a second paper adds statistical guarantees so a self-edit is accepted only when it provably helps.

beats.headline: SciMARS applies recursive harness adaptation to multi-agent scientific discovery
beats.summary: Analysis, experiment design, and verification agents adapt their shared harness task by task in a closed loop.

beats.headline: RSI moves from the harness back into the model
beats.summary: BaseRSI targets harness-bound gains that stay outside the model; Piccolo co-evolves model and data across a 0.8B-27B family.

open_questions: Does Flex-RSI publish per-model scores that show which frontier agents actually gain from editing their own harness?
Do statistical acceptance tests for self-edits hold when the eval distribution shifts after deployment?
Does BaseRSI's training-free internalization keep its gains on tasks outside the harness it learned from?
Do any of these loops report results outside their own benchmark harnesses?
